paper_design_summary: Study 1 is a preregistered online experiment with 310 professors in the US, Canada, and the UK. Each uploaded the title and abstract of a recent paper and was randomly assigned to see no AI suggestion, one GPT-4 research idea, or three GPT-4 research ideas, then drafted a new research idea. Outcomes are the embedding similarity of the drafted idea to the AI suggestion(s) and the participant's own ratings of the idea's novelty, feasibility, and impact; no external rater scored the ideas. Study 2 is a qualitative interview study with 28 researchers who all received an AI suggestion.

studies.label: Study 1: online experiment on research idea generation with GPT-4 suggestions

assignment.what_was_assigned: Whether the participant saw AI-generated research suggestions (none, 1, or 3 GPT-4 suggestions based on the participant's own abstract) before drafting a new research idea
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three conditions. In the "human only" condition, participants were not shown the generated AI suggestion and were asked to provide a new research idea based on their submitted titles and abstracts.
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 4, Section 3.1: https://aspredicted.org/TDR_TS4; novelty and feasibility named as pre-registered outcomes (p. 5, Section 3.1.1); target of 450 participants not reached (p. 4)

arms.name: Human only
arms.description: Shown only their own title and abstract; an AI suggestion was generated but not shown

arms.name: 1 generative AI suggestion
arms.description: Shown one GPT-4 research idea generated from their abstract while drafting

arms.name: 3 generative AI suggestions
arms.description: Shown three GPT-4 research ideas generated from their abstract while drafting

participants.exclusions: Incomplete responses were removed after data collection; the number removed and whether removal followed assignment are not stated. Regressions use 310 (309 for AI suggestion-idea similarity in Table 3); moderation regressions in Table 4 use 294, with no reason stated for the drop.
participants.who: Researchers with job function 'professor' in 'education' drawn from a commercial contact database, all fields; mean experience 30.7 years; 58.1% male
participants.quote: The final response rate for the entire experiment was 0.62%, resulting in 310 participants from various academic fields, short of our pre-registered target.
participants.locator: p. 4, Section 3.1; arm counts p. 5, Fig. 1 and p. 6, Table 1 (Observations 100, 103, 107)

ai_tool.how_used: The participant's title and abstract were sent to GPT-4 with a fixed prompt asking for one future research idea (200 words max); participants did not interact with the AI and saw 1 or 3 generated ideas while drafting (p. 4-5)

task.description: Draft a new research idea for a future project based on one of the participant's recently published papers
task.duration: Participants spent 13 min on average completing the study (p. 5)

outcomes.name: Novelty index (self-assessed)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Participant's own rating of their idea as novel, original, and rare, each on a 9-point scale, averaged into an index (Cronbach's alpha = 0.909). Pre-registered outcome. Components in supplement Tables B3-B5.

contrasts.treatment_arm: Generative AI suggestions (1 and 3 suggestion arms combined)
contrasts.reported: Generative AI suggestions -0.218 (0.194); constant 6.317 (0.157); N = 310; p = 0.262. Moderation (Table 4 col. 2, N = 294): AI x experience -0.040 (0.013), p = 0.003; AI 1.060 (0.445); experience 0.027 (0.010). OLS, robust SE.
contrasts.locator: p. 7, Table 3 col. 2 and Section 4.1.1; p. 8, Table 4 col. 2

outcomes.name: Feasibility index (self-assessed)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Participant's own rating of their idea as appropriate for targeted journals, feasible, and publishable, 9-point scales averaged (Cronbach's alpha = 0.750). Pre-registered outcome.

contrasts.treatment_arm: Generative AI suggestions (1 and 3 suggestion arms combined)
contrasts.reported: Generative AI suggestions -0.121 (0.158); constant 7.403 (0.124); N = 310; p = 0.446. Moderation (Table 4 col. 3, N = 294): AI x experience -0.002 (0.012), p = 0.854.
contrasts.locator: p. 7, Table 3 col. 3 and Section 4.1.1; p. 8, Table 4 col. 3

outcomes.name: Impact index (self-assessed)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Participant's own rating that the idea would be publishable in a top journal, advance the focal field, and advance adjacent fields, 9-point scales averaged (Cronbach's alpha = 0.847). Not pre-registered.

contrasts.treatment_arm: Generative AI suggestions (1 and 3 suggestion arms combined)
contrasts.reported: Generative AI suggestions 0.189 (0.197); constant 6.323 (0.160); N = 310; p = 0.337. Moderation (Table 4 col. 4, N = 294): AI x experience -0.031 (0.014), p = 0.031; AI 1.195 (0.496).
contrasts.locator: p. 7, Table 3 col. 4 and Section 4.1.1; p. 8, Table 4 col. 4

outcomes.name: AI suggestion-idea similarity
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Cosine similarity between word-embedding vectors of the participant's submitted idea and the GPT-4 suggestion(s) generated from that participant's own abstract (averaged over three suggestions in the 3-suggestion arm; computed against the unseen suggestion in the human-only arm). Measures incorporation of the AI suggestion, not creativity and not similarity across different people.

contrasts.treatment_arm: Generative AI suggestions (1 and 3 suggestion arms combined)
contrasts.reported: Generative AI suggestions 6.050*** (1.290); constant 63.372*** (0.872); N = 309; p < 0.001; 'increases the similarity to those suggestions by 9.5%'. Moderation (Table 4 col. 1, N = 294): AI x experience -0.239 (0.088), p = 0.007; AI 13.470 (3.056).

assignment.what_was_assigned: Nothing; all participants received a GPT-5.2 research suggestion and could optionally iterate with the AI
assignment.quote: The study required participants to first ideate with the help of an AI suggestion and then, optionally, further interact with generative AI to improve their submitted research idea.

arms.name: AI suggestion (all participants)
arms.description: One GPT-5.2 suggestion from the uploaded title and abstract, then optional further interaction, followed by a semi-structured interview

participants.who: 21 less experienced and 7 more experienced researchers recruited by the authors through theoretical sampling; experience 2 to 49 years
participants.country: Spain, UK, France, Canada, Denmark, Switzerland, Australia, US, Germany (Table 2)
participants.quote: In total, 28 study participants (21 less experienced and 7 more experienced) took part in this study, and interviews lasted between 35 and 80 min

task.description: Draft a new related research idea, then interview about the ideation process

data_and_code.data_url: OSF; file ai_science_merged_notext.csv, linked from the article page (URL not printed in the PDF)

eligibility.reason: Study 1 randomly assigned 310 analyzed researchers to AI suggestions or none on a research-ideation task, but novelty, feasibility, and impact are the participants' self-ratings of their own ideas (p. 5-6; the authors state 'the outcome in our study was self-assessed', p. 14). The only output-based measure is the embedding similarity of each idea to the AI suggestion made from that person's own abstract, which measures incorporation of the suggestion, not creativity or diversity across people. Study 2 (28 people) has no comparison group and no scored outcome.

one_line_finding: Receiving GPT-4 research suggestions made researchers' ideas more similar to those suggestions (6.050, SE 1.290, N = 309) but did not change self-rated novelty (-0.218, SE 0.194), feasibility (-0.121, SE 0.158), or impact (0.189, SE 0.197) on average (p. 7, Table 3); experience negatively moderated similarity and self-rated novelty and impact (p. 8, Table 4).
open_questions: Whether the AI suggestion-idea similarity measure (embedding similarity to the person's own AI suggestion) should count as an output-scored outcome for any of the three questions; I coded it as answering none.
Number of people randomized before incomplete responses were removed is not stated; the drop from 310 to 294 in Table 4 is not explained in the main text.
notes: Main text pools the 1- and 3-suggestion arms; separate-arm results are in supplement Tables B1-B2 (not in this PDF). Table 4 col. 5 also reports self-reported enjoyment of the exercise (AI x experience -0.033, SE 0.017, p = 0.051), which is not an output outcome and is not listed. Qualitative coding of open-ended comments (Table 5) is not listed. Randomization balance: experience differs between human-only and 1-suggestion arms (33.167 vs 28.615, p = 0.030; Table 1, p. 6).
